dioscorides.excerpt: ἐλελίσφακον· οἱ δὲ ἐλαφοβόσκον, οἱ δὲ σφάγνον. θάμνος ἐστὶν ἐπιμήκης, πολύκλωνος, ῥάβδους τετραγώνους καὶ ὑπολεύκους ἔχων
dioscorides.edition: Wellmann 1906, Pedanii Dioscuridis Anazarbei De materia medica vol. II (libri III-IV), Berlin: Weidmann; read from page scan on archive.org (BIUSante_65865x02), p. 44

identification.source: Sprengel 1830, vol. 2, p. 510 (Comm. III cap. XXXV, ἐλελίσφακον): 'Quaenam salviae species intelligatur, potest omnino ambigi. Vero tamen est haud absimile, Salviam nostram officinalem, quae in asperis omnis Graeciae locis provenit, hac appellatione comprehendi.' Sprengel names Salvia officinalis (tentatively), NOT S. fruticosa; the species is explicitly said to be open to doubt. | Fraas 1845, p. 184: '20. Salvia pomifera L., breitblättriger Salbey (triloba und baccifera sind synonym). Ist die bei weitem häufigste in Griechenland' = σφάκος Theophr., ἐλελίσφακον Diosc. 3,35; also S. calycina L. = ἐλελίσφακον Theophr.; S. officinalis 'Sehr selten!' in Greece. Fraas treats S. triloba (= S. fruticosa) as a synonym within his S. pomifera, so his identification covers S. fruticosa only in that lumped sense. Osbaldeston 2000, ch. 3-40 ELELISPHAKON: SUGGESTED Salvia maior, Salvia minor [Fuchs, Bauhin], Salvia officinalis [Linnaeus]. (https://archive.org/details/BIUSante_dioscsprengelx02/page/n511/mode/1up ; https://archive.org/details/synopsisplantaru00fraa/page/n229/mode/1up)

alternatives.name: Salvia pomifera L. (incl. S. triloba = S. fruticosa, as synonyms)

caveats: Identification is disputed; results describe Salvia fruticosa Mill., which may not be the plant Dioscorides meant.
